answer:
Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic solid mechanics applies.
Assume the shaft is a solid circular cylinder with length L and radius R.
Assume the material is homogeneous and isotropic with shear modulus G.
Assume Saint-Venant torsion applies, so circular cross-sections remain plane and rotate rigidly about the longitudinal axis.
Assume applied torques are concentrated couples acting at discrete axial locations along the shaft.
Assume any transverse shear force is known or is determined from lateral equilibrium.
Define the axial coordinate x along the shaft centerline.
Use the right-hand rule sign convention for torques and angles of twist.
The polar second moment of area of a solid circular cross-section is J = π R^4 / 2, or J = π d^4 / 32 where d is the shaft diameter.
The internal torque T(x) at any cross-section is the algebraic sum of all applied torques on one side of that section.
At a section where a concentrated torque T_i is applied, the internal torque jumps by T_i.
The torsional shear stress at radius r is τ_t(r,x) = T(x) r / J.
The maximum torsional shear stress occurs at the outer surface and is τ_t,max(x) = T(x) R / J.
The torsional shear strain is γ_t(r,x) = τ_t(r,x) / G.
The angle of twist gradient is dφ/dx = T(x) / (G J).
The relative angle of twist between x = a and x = b is φ(b) − φ(a) = ∫_a^b T(x) / (G J) dx.
If the internal torque is constant over each segment, the total relative twist is the sum of T_i L_i / (G J) over all segments.
If the shaft has supports, rotational equilibrium and compatibility of total twist determine the support reactions.
For a transverse shear force V(x), the transverse shear stress at any point in the cross-section is τ_v = V(x) Q / (I b), where Q is the first moment of area, I is the second moment of area about the bending axis, and b is the width of the section at that point.
For a solid circular section, the maximum transverse shear stress occurs at the centroidal axis and is τ_v,max = 4 V(x) / (3 π R^2).
The relevant response quantities to determine are the support reactions, the internal torque diagram, the angle-of-twist diagram, the total angle of twist, the torsional shear stress distribution, the transverse shear stress distribution, and the maximum combined shear stress where both torsional and transverse shear act simultaneously.
When torsional and transverse shear act at the same location, superimpose the shear stress components vectorially to obtain the resultant shear stress.
